terms.name: 60-30-10 rule
terms.definition: A proportion guideline that gives about 60 percent of a layout to a dominant colour, 30 percent to a secondary, and 10 percent to an accent.

terms.name: Activity feed
terms.definition: A reverse chronological list of things that happened, each entry naming an actor, a verb, and an object, grouped when many are alike.

terms.name: Aperture
terms.definition: The partly enclosed opening in a letter, such as the gap where the two terminals of a c stop or the mouth at the bottom of an e.

terms.name: Audio description
terms.definition: A narration track describing visual information the soundtrack leaves out, fitted into the gaps between dialogue.

terms.name: Blame view
terms.definition: Each line of a file labelled with the change that last touched it, so the file answers who and when rather than what it says.

terms.name: Busy state
terms.definition: Marking a region as still loading so assistive technology waits for the finished result instead of reading each row as it streams in.

terms.name: Ch unit
terms.definition: A CSS length equal to the advance width of the digit zero in the current font, used to set column widths in characters rather than pixels.

terms.name: Chunking
terms.definition: Breaking content into small labelled pieces, short paragraphs, lists, and headings, so a reader can hold one piece at a time instead of the whole wall.

terms.name: Color picker
terms.definition: A control for choosing a colour, usually pairing a saturation and lightness field with a hue slider, an alpha slider and a text field for a value.

terms.name: Common region
terms.definition: The grouping principle that anything inside a shared boundary reads as one group, strong enough to beat how far apart the items actually are.

terms.name: Container query
terms.definition: A rule that responds to the size of a component's own container rather than the viewport, so one component adapts anywhere it is placed.

terms.name: Cubic bezier
terms.definition: The four-control-point curve that describes how a value moves between its start and end, the default way CSS spells an easing.

terms.name: Debounce
terms.definition: Waiting until input has stopped for a set moment before reacting, so a burst of keystrokes or clicks produces one response instead of many.

terms.name: Direct manipulation
terms.definition: Acting on an object by handling the object itself, dragging, resizing, or typing into it, rather than describing the change in a separate control.

terms.name: Drag handle
terms.definition: The small gripped area, often drawn as rows of dots or lines, that marks where an item may be picked up and dragged.

terms.name: Earcon
terms.definition: A brief synthesized sound standing for an event, abstract by design, so a rising figure means success only because the interface taught you it does.

terms.name: Error bar
terms.definition: Whiskers on a mark showing the range a value could plausibly take, so a chart does not imply precision it does not have.

terms.name: Fake scarcity
terms.definition: Claiming limited supply that is not real, with stock counts or demand messages generated to pressure a decision rather than report a fact.

terms.name: First run experience
terms.definition: Everything shown only on the very first open, from a welcome sequence to seeded sample content, and never shown to that person again.

terms.name: Focal point
terms.definition: The one element a composition is built around, given enough size, contrast or isolation that the eye lands there before anywhere else.

terms.name: Font stack
terms.definition: The ordered list of typefaces a rule names, each tried in turn until one is available, ending in a generic family.

terms.name: Generative UI
terms.definition: An interface whose parts are chosen or composed by a model at runtime, so a request is answered with a built form, chart, or panel instead of a paragraph of text.

terms.name: Group label
terms.definition: The one name that covers a set of controls, a question above its radio buttons or a heading above an address block, so each field is heard in context.

terms.name: Helper text
terms.definition: The short line under a field that explains the format or constraint before anything goes wrong.

terms.name: HUD panel
terms.definition: A small dark translucent floating window of controls that hovers over content without taking it over, common in media and creative tools.

terms.name: Infinite canvas
terms.definition: A workspace with no page edges, where content is placed anywhere in an unbounded plane and the viewport pans and zooms over it instead of scrolling a document.

terms.name: Invalid state
terms.definition: The programmatic mark that a field's value failed validation, paired with a pointer to the message that explains it.

terms.name: Keyboard shortcut
terms.definition: A key or key combination that runs a command directly, giving practised users a path that skips the menus and the pointer entirely.

terms.name: Layout shifter
terms.definition: A responsive pattern where the arrangement genuinely differs per breakpoint rather than reflowing, so each size gets its own composition.

terms.name: Link
terms.definition: A control that navigates somewhere, named for its destination, and carrying the browser affordances of a destination (open in new tab, copy address).

terms.name: Low poly
terms.definition: A 3D style that keeps the polygon count low enough to see, so surfaces read as faceted triangles under flat shading instead of smooth curves.

terms.name: Mention autocomplete
terms.definition: Typing a trigger character inside a text field to open a filtered list of people or objects, inserting the chosen one as a linked token.

terms.name: Mixed state checkbox
terms.definition: A checkbox showing a third, indeterminate state when only some of the boxes it governs are checked.

terms.name: Motion token
terms.definition: A named duration or easing value published by a design system, so timings are chosen from a set rather than typed per component.

terms.name: Neubrutalism
terms.definition: A loud style built from thick black outlines, saturated flat color, square corners, and hard offset shadows with zero blur.

terms.name: On-color
terms.definition: A colour defined by what it sits on, such as on-primary or on-surface, so every fill ships with the foreground guaranteed to be readable against it.

terms.name: Orphan
terms.definition: A first line of a paragraph left alone at the bottom of a column or page, with the rest of the paragraph carried over.

terms.name: Pane
terms.definition: A layout container that holds one destination's content inside a window, either fixed or flexible in width, combined with other panes to fill the space.

terms.name: Pixel density
terms.definition: How many physical pixels a display packs into an inch, and the reason a CSS pixel is a unit of measure rather than a dot on the screen.

terms.name: Presence indicator
terms.definition: The small coloured dot on an avatar reporting whether a person is available, away, busy or offline.

terms.name: Prompt input
terms.definition: The composer at the bottom of an assistant interface: a growing text area with attachment, model and send controls attached to it.

terms.name: Rage click
terms.definition: A burst of repeated clicks on one spot, the shape frustration takes when a control answers nothing, and the analytics signal that goes looking for it.

terms.name: Reference line
terms.definition: A line drawn at a meaningful value across a chart: a target, a threshold, an average, a before-and-after moment.

terms.name: Risograph style
terms.definition: A print-inspired look of two or three flat spot colors that misregister slightly and show grain, imitating a riso duplicator.

terms.name: Scarcity indicator
terms.definition: A label reporting how little of something is left, in stock, in seats, or in time, placed beside the action it is meant to accelerate.

terms.name: Scrollbar color
terms.definition: The thumb and track colours of a scrollbar, which a page can set explicitly or leave to the declared colour scheme so the browser draws its own dark variant.

terms.name: Sensory characteristics
terms.definition: Instructions that lean on shape, size, position, or sound alone, such as the round button on the right, which fail when those cues are not perceived.

terms.name: Situational disability
terms.definition: A barrier that comes from the moment rather than the body, one arm holding a baby, sunlight on a screen, a noisy train, and that makes the audience for access everyone.

terms.name: Social proof
terms.definition: Showing what other people did or said next to a decision, as counts, reviews, logos, or live activity, so the reader can borrow their judgement.

terms.name: Split view
terms.definition: A layout of two or more side by side panes where a choice in the leading pane decides what the trailing pane shows.

terms.name: Status message
terms.definition: A change in content that reports progress, result, or state and must be announced without taking focus, such as a count of search results.

terms.name: Subject line
terms.definition: The one line a mail is opened or ignored on, written to survive a list that truncates it and shows it wedged between the sender and the preview text.

terms.name: Syntax highlighting
terms.definition: Colouring code by what each token is, keyword or string or comment or name, so the structure and the typo are visible before a line has actually been read.

terms.name: Text balancing
terms.definition: Choosing line breaks so a short block of text has lines of roughly equal length instead of a long first line and a stub second one.

terms.name: Title case
terms.definition: Capitalising the first letter of each significant word in a heading or label, leaving short articles, conjunctions and prepositions lowercase.

terms.name: Transparency checkerboard
terms.definition: The light grey and white checker grid a design tool paints behind transparent regions, a convention so universal that the pattern itself now reads as meaning alpha.

terms.name: Typography token
terms.definition: A named bundle of type values (family, size, weight, line height, tracking) that a design system hands out instead of raw numbers.

terms.name: Video player
terms.definition: A framed video with the controls needed to play, seek, mute and caption it, sized so the controls never crowd the picture.

terms.name: Window controls
terms.definition: The cluster of close, minimise and zoom controls in a window's title bar, three coloured dots on macOS and three glyphs on Windows.
